History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
32-year-old male* with 4-day history of sore throat, rhinorrhea, new dry cough, congestion, night sweats, myalgias, and intermittent headache – most consistent with a self-limiting viral upper respiratory tract infection / influenza-like illness.

(*Age not stated; patient described as adult male.)

History:
• Presenting complaint: 4 days of upper-respiratory symptoms.  
• Timeline  
  – Day 0: Exposed to ill co-worker’s respiratory symptoms.  
  – Days 1-2: Developed painful sore throat (odynophagia), clear rhinorrhea, subjective fever.  
  – Day 3: Throat pain improving; ongoing nasal congestion; onset of night sweats, myalgias, intermittent generalized headaches.  
  – Day 4 (today): New constant dry cough; continues to feel fatigued and “winded” on exertion; afebrile after paracetamol/ibuprofen.  
• Exacerbating / relieving factors: Antipyretics (paracetamol, ibuprofen) reduce fever. Rest helps.  
• Associated symptoms  
  – Present: Nasal congestion, fatigue, night sweats, exertional dyspnea (none at rest), muscle aches, decreased appetite, ↑ fluid intake.  
  – Denied: Chest pain, resting dyspnea, ear pain/discharge, photophobia, visual changes, nausea, vomiting, bowel or urinary disturbance, skin rash.  
• Review of systems: As above; all other systems unremarkable.

Past Medical History:
• No chronic medical conditions reported.  
• No regular medications.  
• Current symptomatic medications:  
  – Paracetamol – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
  – Ibuprofen – dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
• No known drug allergies.

Social History:
• Lives alone.  
• Occupation: Accountant; currently working but performance slowed; increased work stress (described as “good stress”).  
• Tobacco: Occasional cigars at company parties (non-daily).  
• Alcohol: Occasional social use; “not a very big drinker.”  
• Recreational drugs: Not mentioned.  

Family History:
• Maternal grandmother – type 2 diabetes mellitus.  
• Great-grandfather – eczema.  
• No other significant familial conditions reported.

Physical Examination:
(Not performed during tele-consult; no vitals available.)

Investigations:
• None ordered or reviewed.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Viral upper respiratory tract infection / early influenza-like illness  
  – Self-limiting course expected (≈7 days).  
  – Plan:  
    • Rest; advised 1–2 days off work.  
    • Oral hydration (“push fluids”).  
    • Continue paracetamol and/or ibuprofen as needed for fever, pain (ensure dosing within OTC guidelines).  
    • Return precautions: seek review sooner for high fever, worsening cough, new chest pain, or increasing breathlessness; routine follow-up if not improved by next week.

General plan items  
  – Encourage smoking cessation; limit cigar use.  
  – Re-emphasize infection-control practices (hand hygiene, avoid close contact while symptomatic).  
  – Offer future review for work-related stress or mood concerns if needed.

Quality checks:
• Missing expected elements: age, vitals, physical examination, medication doses/frequency, vaccination status (e.g., influenza), COVID-19 screening not discussed.  
• No internal transcript conflicts noted.
